items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the amount of cash dividend distributed to shareholders. If no dividend is declared, the default value is 0.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the adjusted closing price of stocks, which accounts for corporate actions such as stock splits and dividends, providing a more accurate reflection of the stock's value over time.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the adjusted high price of stocks, reflecting the highest price reached during a trading session after accounting for factors such as stock splits and dividends.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable provides an integer representation of industries, encompassing approximately 70 distinct industries. Each integer corresponds to a specific industry category, facilitating industry-based analysis and comparisons.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the adjusted low price of stocks, accounting for factors such as stock splits and dividends. It reflects the lowest price at which a stock traded during a specific period, adjusted to provide a more accurate historical comparison.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the market capitalization of stocks, calculated by multiplying the stock's current price by the total number of outstanding shares. Market capitalization is a key indicator of a company's size and market value.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the adjusted opening price of stocks, reflecting the price at which a stock begins trading at the start of a trading session, adjusted for factors such as stock splits and dividends.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable provides the integer representation of sectors as classified, encompassing approximately 13 distinct sectors. Each integer corresponds to a specific sector, facilitating categorization and analysis of financial data based on sector performance.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the number of floating shares available for trading, expressed in millions. Floating shares are those that are publicly owned and can be traded on the open market, excluding restricted shares held by insiders or company executives.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the total number of outstanding shares of a company, expressed in millions. Outstanding shares are the shares currently held by all shareholders, including institutional investors and company insiders, and are used to calculate key financial metrics such as Earnings Per Share (EPS).

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable provides an integer representation of subindustries, categorizing companies into approximately 500 distinct subindustry classifications. This classification aids in sector analysis and comparison within the financial markets.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the total composite trading volume, which includes all trading activity during the session, encompassing both open and close auction volumes. The term 'composite' refers to the aggregation of all trading volumes, providing a comprehensive measure of market activity.

items.author: tpark|aarnold|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the 1-day return of a stock, calculated as the percentage change from the previous day's closing price to today's closing price. It is computed using the formula: (close_today - close_yesterday) / close_yesterday.

items.author: tpark|aarnold|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the 10-day return, calculated as the percentage change in the stock's closing price over the last 10 days. It is computed using the formula: (close_today - close_10_days_ago) / close_10_days_ago.

items.author: tpark|aarnold|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the 20-day return, calculated as the percentage change in the stock's closing price over the last 20 days. It is computed using the formula: (close_today - close_20d_ago) / close_20d_ago, where 'close_today' is the closing price on the current day and 'close_20d_ago' is the closing price 20 days prior.

items.author: tpark|aarnold|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the 5-day return of a stock, calculated as the percentage change between today's closing price and the closing price from 5 days ago. The formula used is (close_today - close_5d_ago) / close_5d_ago.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. AOCI includes unrealized gains and losses on certain investments and foreign currency translation adjustments that are not included in net income.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the amortization expense related to intangible assets as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Amortization of intangible assets reflects the gradual write-off of the cost of intangible assets over their useful life.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the current portion of long-term debt as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It indicates the amount of long-term debt that is due within the next year.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the long-term Deferred Tax Assets as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Deferred Tax Assets arise when a company has overpaid taxes or has tax losses that can be used to reduce future tax liabilities.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total Depreciation and Amortization expenses as reported in the Income Statement of a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. These expenses reflect the systematic allocation of the cost of tangible and intangible assets over their useful lives.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable measures the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on cash and cash equivalents as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects how changes in foreign currency exchange rates affect the value of cash holdings, quantifying the effect in terms of cash increase or decrease caused by these fluctuations. The value is reported in millions, providing a clear understanding of the financial impact on the company's liquidity.
items.keywords: Effect of Exchange Rate Changes on Cash

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Gross Profit as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Gross Profit is calculated as total revenue minus the cost of goods sold (COGS), reflecting the profitability of a company's core business activities before accounting for operating expenses, taxes, and interest.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Long Term Debt as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Long Term Debt includes all debt obligations that are due beyond one year from the reporting date.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Net Sales as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Net Sales is the total revenue from goods sold or services provided, minus returns, allowances, and discounts.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the value of short-term investments as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Short-term investments are financial assets that are expected to be converted into cash or sold within one year or within the operating cycle, whichever is longer.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of stock-based compensation reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Stock-based compensation includes equity awards such as stock options and restricted stock units granted to employees and executives as part of their remuneration.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total deposits reported by a company in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Total deposits include all customer deposits held by the institution, reflecting its liquidity position and funding sources.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total operating expenses as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Operating expenses include all costs associated with running the business, excluding costs of goods sold (COGS).

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total value of Accounts and Notes Receivable as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes amounts owed to the company by customers and other parties for goods or services provided.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of Accounts Payable as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Accounts Payable refers to the liabilities a company owes to its suppliers for goods and services received but not yet paid for.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total Accounts Receivable for a company as reported in its Form 8-K filings, excluding any amounts classified as Notes Receivable. It provides insight into the company's receivables that are expected to be collected in the short term, without the influence of longer-term notes.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the accumulated depreciation as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Accumulated depreciation reflects the total depreciation expense that has been allocated to an asset over its useful life, reducing its book value on the balance sheet.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Additional Paid-in Capital (APIC) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. APIC is the amount received from shareholders in excess of the par value of the stock, reflecting the additional funds contributed by investors.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the amount of Treasury Stock reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Treasury Stock refers to shares that were once a part of the outstanding shares but were later repurchased by the company and are held in the company's treasury.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of cash and near cash items reported in a company's balance sheet as disclosed in their Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Near cash items typically include assets that are easily convertible to cash, such as short-term investments and marketable securities. This definition aligns with industry standards, which classify near cash items as liquid assets that can be quickly converted to cash, excluding restricted cash.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the value of collaterals held in cash and cash equivalents, including marketable securities and short-term investments, as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total value of common stocks as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Common stocks represent ownership in a company and entitle shareholders to vote on corporate matters and receive dividends.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total current assets reported by a company in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Current assets include cash, accounts receivable, inventory, and other assets expected to be converted into cash or used within one year.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Current Liabilities as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Current Liabilities include obligations that are due to be settled within one year, such as accounts payable, short-term debt, and other similar liabilities.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Deferred Tax Liabilities as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Deferred Tax Liabilities arise when a company has a tax expense that is recognized on the income statement but not yet paid, indicating future tax obligations.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the amount of Goodwill reported in a company's balance sheet as disclosed in their Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Goodwill is an intangible asset that arises when a company acquires another business for a premium over its fair value, reflecting factors such as brand reputation, customer relationships, and intellectual property.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total inventories reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes all goods available for sale and raw materials held by the company at the reporting date.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of long-term borrowings reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Long-term borrowings are financial obligations that are due beyond one year, typically used to finance long-term investments or operations.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total value of marketable securities and other short-term investments as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. These assets are typically liquid and can be easily converted into cash within a year.
items.keywords: marketable securities and other short-term investments

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the value of Other Current Assets as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. This category includes assets that are expected to be converted into cash or used up within one year, excluding specific line items such as cash, accounts receivable, and inventory.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of Other Long Term Liabilities reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. This category includes liabilities that are not classified under standard long-term liabilities, providing insight into additional financial obligations that may impact the company's long-term financial health.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of other short-term liabilities reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. These liabilities are obligations that are due within one year and are not classified under standard categories such as accounts payable or accrued expenses.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Pure Retained Earnings as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Pure Retained Earnings refer to the cumulative amount of net income that has been retained in the company rather than distributed as dividends, excluding any adjustments or reclassifications. This figure reflects the company's ability to reinvest profits back into the business, which can be crucial for growth and financial stability.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of retained earnings and other equity components as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Retained earnings reflect the cumulative profits that have been reinvested in the business rather than distributed as dividends, while other equity may include additional paid-in capital and other comprehensive income.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of short-term borrowings reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Short-term borrowings typically include loans and financial obligations that are due within one year.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Total Assets as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Total Assets encompass all resources owned by the company that have economic value.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Total Equity or Partnership Capital as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It encompasses the total value of equity held by shareholders or partners, reflecting the net assets of the company after liabilities are deducted.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total liabilities as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Total liabilities encompass all financial obligations a company owes to outside parties, including loans, accounts payable, and other debts.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total value of Other Property and Equipment as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. This includes assets that are not classified as current assets or fixed assets, such as machinery, furniture, and leasehold improvements.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of Accounts Payable and Accruals as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the liabilities a company owes to suppliers and other creditors for goods and services received but not yet paid for, as well as accrued expenses that have been recognized but not yet settled.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the capital expenditures related to property additions as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes investments made by the company to acquire or improve physical assets, which are essential for long-term operational capacity and growth.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the cash flow generated from financing activities as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes cash inflows and outflows related to transactions involving equity and debt financing.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the cash flow generated or used in investing activities as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes cash transactions related to the acquisition and disposal of long-term assets, investments in securities, and other investment-related cash flows.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Cash From Operations as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It indicates the cash generated from the company's core business operations, excluding cash flows from investing and financing activities.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the change in inventories as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It indicates the difference in inventory levels over a specified period, reflecting the company's operational adjustments and inventory management strategies.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the amount of Deferred Income Taxes as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Deferred Income Taxes arise from temporary differences between the accounting and tax treatment of income and expenses, leading to future tax liabilities or assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of Depreciation and Amortization expenses reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Depreciation refers to the allocation of the cost of tangible assets over their useful lives, while amortization pertains to the gradual write-off of intangible assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of dividends paid by the company as reported in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the net changes in cash as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the total increase or decrease in cash and cash equivalents during the reporting period.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Cash Flow from Net Income as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the net income adjusted for non-cash items and changes in working capital, providing insight into the actual cash generated by the company's operations.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the value of Intangible and Other Assets as reported in a company's Balance Sheet filed with the SEC. This category includes non-physical assets such as goodwill, patents, trademarks, and other intangible resources that contribute to the company's value.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Interest Income reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes income earned from interest on loans, investments, and other financial assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Adjusted Net Income as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Adjusted Net Income typically excludes certain one-time expenses or income to provide a clearer picture of ongoing profitability, reflecting net income from continuing operations before the effects of one-time gains and losses as disclosed by the company. The method of adjustment may vary by company and can be specific to particular countries and industries.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the average number of shares outstanding used in the calculation of Earnings Per Share (EPS) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC.
items.keywords: Average Number of Shares for EPS

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the direct costs attributable to the production of the goods sold by the company, including fixed expenses and general production costs.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Diluted EPS accounts for the potential dilution of shares that could occur if convertible securities were exercised or options were granted, providing a more conservative view of earnings per share.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Dividend Per Share (DPS) as reported in a company’s Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It indicates the amount of cash dividend distributed to each outstanding share of common stock.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Basic Earnings Per Share (EPS) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It is calculated by dividing net income by the weighted average number of shares outstanding.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the General and Administrative Expenses as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. These expenses include costs related to the overall administration of the business, such as salaries, office supplies, and utilities.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Income Tax Expenses (or Credits) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes both expenses incurred and any tax credits received during the reporting period, specifically focusing on income taxes resulting from federal, local, or foreign income, including deferred income taxes.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Interest Expense as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the cost incurred by the company for borrowed funds during the reporting period.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Net Interest Expense as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the total interest expense incurred by the company minus any interest income earned during the reporting period.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Operating Income or Loss as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the profit or loss generated from the company's core business operations, excluding any income derived from non-operating activities such as investments or sales of assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the operating (trading) profits generated from discontinued operations as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the financial performance of segments of the business that are no longer active.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total personnel expenses reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes all costs associated with employee compensation, benefits, and related expenses.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Research and Development (R&D) Expense as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the costs incurred in the development of new products or services and improvements to existing offerings.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Diluted Weighted Average Shares outstanding, which accounts for all potential shares that could be created through the conversion of convertible securities, stock options, and other dilutive instruments, as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Total Operating Expenses as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It includes all costs associated with the normal operations of the business, excluding non-operating expenses.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the credits associated with Minority or Non-Controlling Interests as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. These credits reflect the portion of equity in a subsidiary not attributable to the parent company, indicating the financial interests of minority shareholders.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the value of Minority or Non-Controlling Interest as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the portion of equity ownership in a subsidiary not attributable to the parent company, indicating the interests of minority shareholders in the subsidiary's net assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Net Income or Net Profit (Loss) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the total earnings of the company after all expenses, taxes, and costs have been deducted from total revenue.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Net Income Before Minority (Non-controlling) Interest as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the total income attributable to the shareholders before accounting for the share of income that is attributable to minority interests.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Net Interest Income as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Net Interest Income is the difference between the revenue generated from interest-bearing assets and the expenses associated with paying interest on liabilities.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Net Interest Income after provisions as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the income generated from interest-bearing assets after accounting for provisions for loan losses.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total amount of non-current liabilities as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Non-current liabilities are obligations that are not due to be settled within one year or within the company's operating cycle, whichever is longer.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Non-Interest Expense as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Non-Interest Expenses include all expenses incurred by the company that are not related to interest payments, such as operating expenses, administrative costs, salaries, employee benefits, occupancy expenses, depreciation, and marketing costs.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Non-Interest Income reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Non-Interest Income includes all income generated by a financial institution that is not derived from interest on loans or investments, such as fees, commissions, and other revenue sources.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total value of other assets as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. This category includes assets that do not fall under standard classifications such as cash, receivables, or inventory, and may encompass various types of investments or intangible assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Pre-Tax Income as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Pre-Tax Income is calculated as total revenue minus total expenses, excluding taxes.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the revenue generated by a company as reported in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the total sales revenue over a specified period, indicating the company's ability to generate income from its operations.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Tangible Equity as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. Tangible Equity is calculated as total equity minus intangible assets, providing a measure of the company's net worth based solely on its tangible assets.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the total liabilities and equity as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It encompasses all financial obligations and the shareholders' equity, providing a comprehensive view of the company's financial position.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the Total Shareholders' Equity as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It reflects the net assets owned by shareholders, calculated as total assets minus total liabilities.

items.author: wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|wdeng|ctseng
items.description: This variable represents the changes in Working Capital as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC, reflecting cash flow impacts from operational activities. Changes in Working Capital are calculated as the difference between current assets and current liabilities, indicating how operational activities affect cash flow.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in Accounts Receivable from the previous year to the current year, indicating the growth rate of receivables over that period.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the annual return on equity (ROE) expressed as a percentage, assessing a company's profit in relation to the equity invested by shareholders. It provides insight into how effectively a company is using shareholders' funds to generate profit.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the company's non-cash working capital, calculated as Current Assets minus Cash and Current Liabilities. It provides insight into the liquidity available for operational needs, excluding cash holdings.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of cash and cash equivalents to total liabilities, expressed as a percentage. It provides insight into a company's liquidity position relative to its total obligations as reported in Form 8-K filings with the SEC.
items.keywords: Cash and cash equivalents to total liabilities ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable includes cash and liquid securities that can be quickly converted into cash at a reasonable price. It is calculated as the sum of Cash & Near Cash Items, Marketable Securities & Short-Term Investments, and Long-Term Marketable Securities.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: Cash Flow Growth is calculated as the percentage change in Cash Flow from Operations, using the formula: [(Cash Flow from Operations Current Period - Cash Flow from Operations Same Period Prior Year) / abs(Cash Flow from Operations Same Period Prior Year)] * 100. This metric indicates the growth rate of cash flow generated from operations compared to the same period in the previous year.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures a firm's financial strength by representing the net cash generated by the firm on a per share basis. It provides insight into the company's ability to generate cash relative to its outstanding shares, which is crucial for assessing liquidity and operational efficiency.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of cash flow to total liabilities, indicating the company's ability to cover its liabilities with its cash flow. A higher ratio suggests better financial health and liquidity.
items.keywords: Cash Flow to Total Liabilities Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This ratio measures the cash generated from operations relative to the cash paid for operations during the specified period. It provides insight into a company's operational efficiency and liquidity by comparing cash inflows from operational activities to cash outflows required for those activities.
items.keywords: Cash Generation to Cash Requirements Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: The Cash Ratio is a liquidity metric calculated by dividing the sum of Cash and Near Cash Items plus Marketable Securities by Current Liabilities. This ratio measures a company's ability to cover its short-term obligations with its most liquid assets.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the amount of cash and marketable securities available per share, as reported in a company’s Form 8-K filings with the SEC.
items.keywords: Cash and Marketable Securities per Share

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage of cash and near cash items, along with marketable securities, relative to total current assets. It is calculated using the formula: ((Cash & Near Cash Items + Marketable Securities) / Current Assets) * 100.
items.keywords: Cash and Near Cash Investments to Current Assets Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of cash and near-cash assets to total assets, indicating the percentage of total assets that are liquid or easily convertible to cash. This metric helps assess a company's liquidity position and financial health.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures financial performance by calculating Free Cash Flow, which is derived from operating cash flow minus capital expenditures. It reflects the cash available to the company after maintaining or expanding its asset base, indicating the company's ability to generate cash after accounting for necessary investments.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the percentage of Cash Flow from Operations relative to Sales, indicating the efficiency of a company's operational cash generation compared to its revenue.
items.keywords: Cash Flow from Operations to Sales ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Trailing 12-month Cash From Operations to the total of Short- and Long-Term Borrowings. It provides insight into a company's ability to cover its debt obligations with cash generated from operations over the past year.
items.keywords: Cash From Operations to Total Debt Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This ratio measures the percentage of total current assets relative to total assets, providing insight into the liquidity position of a company as reported in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC.
items.keywords: Current Assets to Total Assets Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of a company's total debt to its market capitalization, providing a measure of financial leverage relative to the company's market size. It is calculated by dividing Total Debt by Market Capitalization.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) margin, a key profitability metric calculated as the ratio of Trailing 12 Months Operating Income (or Loss) to Trailing 12 Months Net Sales, expressed as a percentage. It indicates how efficiently a company generates profit from its sales before accounting for interest and taxes.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) margin of the company, calculated as EBIT divided by net sales. It indicates the company's operational profitability relative to its sales revenue.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) from the previous year to the current year, indicating the growth rate of EBIT over a one-year period.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) from the previous year to the current year. It provides insight into the company's operational performance and profitability over the specified period.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage margin of trailing twelve-month Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) divided by the trailing twelve-month Sales. It provides insight into a company's operational profitability relative to its sales over the past year.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) calculated on a per diluted share basis, as reported in a company’s Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the relationship between Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) and Revenue, expressed as a percentage. It provides insight into a company's operational efficiency by indicating how much of its revenue is converted into EBITDA.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in Earnings Per Share (EPS) before extraordinary items, comparing the current period to the same period in the prior year. It indicates the growth rate of a company's earnings, providing insight into its financial performance over time.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures a company's financial flexibility by calculating Free Cash Flow per Share. It is determined by dividing the total free cash flow by the weighted average number of shares outstanding, providing insight into the cash available for distribution to shareholders after capital expenditures.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in income tax expense from the previous year to the current year, indicating how the company's tax obligations have evolved over the specified period.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in interest expense from the previous year to the current year, indicating how much interest costs have increased or decreased over the year.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the percentage of inventories relative to total current assets, indicating the proportion of current assets that are tied up in inventory.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the percentage of inventories relative to total current assets, providing insight into the proportion of current assets that are tied up in inventory.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of inventories to total assets, measuring the percentage of a company's assets that are held in inventory. It provides insight into how much of the company's resources are tied up in inventory relative to its overall asset base.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in inventory levels from the previous year to the current year, indicating how inventory has increased or decreased over the specified period.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the year-on-year change in Long Term Debt as reported in a company’s Form 8-K filings with the SEC, comparing the current year's Long Term Debt to that of the prior year.
items.keywords: Net Change in Long Term Debt

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the net debt of a company as reported in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It is calculated by subtracting a company's cash and cash equivalents from its total liabilities, providing insight into the company's overall debt situation.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures a company's ability to pay off its net debt using its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA). A lower ratio indicates better financial health and greater capacity to manage debt obligations, with a typical healthy ratio being below 3.0, though this can vary by industry.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This leverage ratio indicates a company's ability to pay off its net debt using operating earnings after accounting for capital expenditures (CAPEX). It provides insight into the financial health and leverage of the company, showing how well earnings can cover net debt obligations post-investment in capital assets.
items.keywords: Net Debt to EBITDA after CAPEX

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of net debt to shareholders' equity, providing insight into a company's financial leverage and capital structure as reported in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC.
items.keywords: Net Debt to Shareholders' Equity Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in net income, calculated by comparing the current period's net income to that of the same period in the prior year.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of net income to the number of employees, providing a measure of profitability on a per-employee basis as reported in a company’s Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the normalized Return on Equity (ROE), calculated using the formula: (Trailing 12 Month Basic Earnings Per Share from Continuing Operations divided by Book Value per Share) multiplied by 100. This metric provides insight into a company's profitability relative to its equity base over the trailing twelve months.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in operating income, calculated by comparing the current period's operating income to that of the same period in the prior year.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures a firm's profitability by calculating Operating Income per Share, excluding non-operating expenses such as interest and taxes. It provides insight into the core operational efficiency of the company on a per-share basis, allowing for better comparison among firms.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Operating Income to Current Liabilities, providing insight into a company's ability to cover its short-term obligations with its operating income.
items.keywords: Operating Income to Current Liabilities Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Operating Income to Long Term Debt, providing insight into a company's ability to cover its long-term debt obligations with its operating income.
items.keywords: Operating Income to Long Term Debt ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Operating Income to Total Debt, calculated as Operating Income divided by the sum of Short Term Debt and Long Term Debt. This metric provides insight into a company's ability to cover its total debt obligations with its operating income.
items.keywords: Operating Income to Total Debt Ratio

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Operating Margin, a financial metric used to assess a company's pricing strategy and operating efficiency, expressed as a percentage. It is calculated by dividing Operating Income (or Losses) by Total Revenue and multiplying by 100.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of pre-tax income calculated on a per-share basis, providing insight into a company's profitability before tax obligations are considered.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the percentage change in pre-tax income from the previous year to the current year, indicating the growth rate of a company's earnings before tax over a one-year period.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents a company's pretax margin, calculated as earnings before tax expressed as a percentage of total sales or revenues. It provides insight into the profitability of a company before accounting for tax expenses.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the company's profitability by comparing the amount of revenue retained as income during the period. It is calculated as (Net Income / Revenue) * 100, expressed as a percentage.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Price to Net Tangible Assets per Share ratio, which compares the stock price to the tangible book value per share. It is a financial metric used to assess the valuation of a company's tangible assets relative to its market price.
items.keywords: Price to Tangible Book Value per Share

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Quick Ratio, a financial metric that indicates a company's ability to meet its short-term liabilities using its most liquid assets. It is calculated as the sum of Cash and Near Cash, Short Term Investments, and Accounts Receivable divided by Current Liabilities.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the amount of net income (or loss) available for reinvestment after deducting total preferred and common dividends. It reflects the earnings retained in the company for growth and expansion purposes.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of retained earnings and other equity to total liabilities and equity, providing insight into a company's financial leverage and equity structure as reported in Form 8-K filings with the SEC. The term 'other equity' includes components such as additional paid-in capital and accumulated other comprehensive income, which are essential for understanding the overall equity position of the company.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures a corporation's profitability by indicating how much profit a company generates with the money shareholders have invested, expressed as a percentage. It reflects the efficiency of the company in utilizing equity to generate earnings.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Return on Assets (ROA), indicating how profitable a company is relative to its total assets, expressed as a percentage. It is calculated as: (Trailing 12-Month Net Income / Average Total Assets) * 100. For the adjusted value that excludes the impact of abnormal items, please reference 'Return on Assets Adjusted' (F1170 RETURN_ON_ASSETS_ADJUSTED).

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Return on Assets (ROA) calculated based on the bottom-line Earnings Per Share (EPS), expressed as a percentage. It measures how effectively a company is using its assets to generate earnings, specifically focusing on net income derived from the bottom EPS. The calculation is done using the formula: Net Income / Average Total Assets * 100.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the cash and near-cash turnover ratio, which measures how effectively a company is utilizing its cash resources in relation to its sales. A higher ratio indicates better efficiency in converting cash into sales revenue.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: The Other Assets Turnover Ratio measures the efficiency with which a company utilizes its other assets to generate revenue. It is calculated by dividing total sales by the value of other assets, providing insight into how effectively the company is leveraging its non-core assets to produce income.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the total debt of a company, calculated as the sum of both short-term and long-term debt as reported in its Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Trailing Twelve Months (T12M) Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) from Continuing Operations, calculated by summing the diluted EPS for the last four quarters, including adjustments for semi-annual or annual reporting periods. The term 'Adjusted' refers to modifications made to the EPS figures to account for specific factors affecting the earnings, ensuring a more accurate representation of ongoing operational performance.
items.keywords: T12M Diluted EPS from Continuing Operations

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Trailing Twelve Months (TTM) Cash Flow per Share, calculated by summing the Cash Flow per Share for the last four quarters reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC.
items.keywords: Trailing Twelve Months Cash Flow per Share

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Trailing Twelve Months (TTM) Cash From Operations, calculated by summing the Cash From Operations figures from the statement of cash flows over the last four quarters. This metric provides insight into the cash generated by a company's core operating activities over the past year.
items.keywords: Trailing Twelve Months Cash From Operations

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This field represents the trailing 12-month diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) from continuing operations, providing a measure of a company's profitability over the past year, adjusted for shares outstanding.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Trailing 12-Month Operating Margin, calculated by dividing the Trailing 12-Month Operating Income by Trailing 12-Month Net Sales and multiplying the result by 100 to express it as a percentage.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This field represents the Earnings Yield, calculated as the reciprocal of the Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio, indicating the earnings generated per dollar of investment in the company's stock.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the company's earnings per share (EPS) expressed as a percentage of its current share price, providing insight into the earnings yield over time as reported in Form 8-K filings with the SEC.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable measures the Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) yield, calculated as the percentage of Trailing 12-month Operating Income per Share relative to its current Trading Price. It provides insight into the profitability of a company in relation to its market valuation.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of enterprise value (EV) to market capitalization (MKT CAP) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. This ratio provides insight into the relative valuation of a company by comparing its total value (including debt and excluding cash) to its market value as determined by its stock price.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the enterprise value (EV) as a multiple of the trailing twelve months (T12M) cash flow from operations, as reported in a company’s Form 8-K filings with the SEC. It provides insight into how the market values the company relative to its operational cash generation.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the enterprise value (EV) as a multiple of the trailing twelve months (T12M) earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT), providing a measure of the company's valuation relative to its operating performance over the past year.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Enterprise Value (EV) to Trailing 12-Month (T12M) Net Income. It is calculated by dividing the Enterprise Value by the net income over the last twelve months, providing insight into the valuation of a company relative to its earnings.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio calculated as the stock's highest price divided by its earnings per share (EPS). It provides insight into how much investors are willing to pay per dollar of earnings, indicating the stock's valuation relative to its earnings.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: This variable represents the low price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of a stock, calculated by dividing the stock's lowest price by its earnings per share (EPS). This ratio provides insight into the valuation of the stock relative to its earnings, indicating how much investors are willing to pay per dollar of earnings.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: The price to cash flow ratio is calculated by dividing a stock's price by its cash flow per share. This ratio is used to evaluate the relative value of a company's stock, indicating how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of cash flow generated by the company.

items.author: yyoo
items.description: The Price to Sales (P/S) ratio is calculated by dividing a stock's last price by its sales per share. This ratio provides insight into how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of sales, helping to assess the valuation of a company relative to its sales performance.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of total assets to shareholders' equity, calculated by dividing total assets by total equity. This ratio provides insight into a company's financial leverage and capital structure.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable measures the ratio of cash flow from operations to total interest expenses incurred during the reporting period. It provides insight into a company's ability to cover its interest obligations with cash generated from its core operations.
items.keywords: Cash Flow to Interest Expense Ratio

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the Cash Flow to Net Income Ratio, indicating the proportion of a company's total net income that is available as cash for investing and financing ongoing business operations. A higher ratio suggests better liquidity and cash availability relative to net income.
items.keywords: Cash Flow to Net Income Ratio

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the Times Interest Earned (TIE) ratio, also known as the Interest Coverage Ratio. It measures the number of times a company can cover its interest payments with its earnings before interest and taxes (EBT plus interest incurred). A higher ratio indicates a greater ability to meet interest obligations.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Enterprise Value (EV) to the Trailing 12 Months (T12M) Free Cash Flow. It provides insight into how the market values a company's cash generation capabilities over the past year, indicating the relative valuation of the company based on its free cash flow. The term 'Periodic' refers to the most recent reporting period, which can be quarterly, semi-annual, or annual, ensuring that the data reflects the latest available information.
items.keywords: EV to T12M Free Cash Flow ratio

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Free Cash Flow (FCF) to Total Debt, calculated as the trailing twelve months (T12M) free cash flow divided by the sum of short-term and long-term debt. This metric provides insight into a company's ability to cover its debt obligations with its available cash flow.
items.keywords: Free Cash Flow to Total Debt ratio

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable measures the percentage of inventories relative to working capital, indicating the proportion of working capital that is tied up in inventory. A higher percentage may suggest potential liquidity issues, while a lower percentage may indicate more efficient working capital management.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the Price to Book Ratio, which is the ratio of the stock price to the book value per share. It is a financial metric used to evaluate a company's market value relative to its book value, indicating how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of net assets.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the Price to EBITDA ratio, calculated by dividing the market price per share by the Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) per share. This ratio is commonly used to evaluate a company's valuation relative to its earnings capacity, with EBITDA per share calculated on a trailing twelve-month basis where available.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the Price to Free Cash Flow ratio, calculated by dividing the period-end stock price by the Trailing 12-month Free Cash Flow per share. This ratio provides insight into how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of free cash flow generated by the company.
items.keywords: Price to Free Cash Flow ratio

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of a company's sales to its marketable securities, indicating how effectively a company is utilizing its marketable securities in relation to its sales revenue.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of a company's sales to its total assets, indicating how efficiently a company utilizes its assets to generate sales. It is a key financial metric used to assess asset efficiency and operational performance.

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This ratio measures the efficiency of a company's management by comparing Selling and Administrative Expenses to Net Sales. It provides insight into how well a company controls its operating expenses relative to its revenue generation.
items.keywords: Operating Expenses to Net Sales Ratio

items.author: hgupta|ssrivastava|kkumar|ameshram|knemchek|lhan|nelango52|rkushwaha|zliu
items.description: This variable represents the ratio of Total Debt to Enterprise Value (EV) as reported in a company's Form 8-K filings with the SEC. This ratio provides insight into the company's leverage and financial risk by comparing its total debt obligations to its overall market value, including equity and debt. The data is based on the most recent reporting period, which can be quarterly, semi-annual, or annual.

items.author: ylu|wdeng
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the last Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
items.keywords: Trading days since last FOMC meeting

items.author: ylu|wdeng
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which is significant for monetary policy decisions and market expectations.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the last trade price of an asset during the afternoon trading session, providing insight into the asset's value at the end of that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: The last trade price recorded after the first hour of trading in the morning session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: The highest price of the asset during the afternoon trading session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the highest price reached during the first hour of trading in the morning session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: Return information ratio during the last hour of trading.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: Return information ratio during the first hour of trading.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the lowest price recorded during the last hour of trading, providing insight into the asset's price behavior in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the lowest price recorded during the first hour of trading, providing insight into the asset's price behavior in the early trading session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the total number of trades executed during the last hour of the trading session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the total number of trades executed during the first hour of trading in the morning session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: The opening price of the asset during the last hour of trading.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: The opening price of the asset during the first hour of trading.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the return generated during the last hour of trading, capturing the asset's performance in that specific time frame.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the return generated during the first hour of trading, capturing the performance of the asset in that initial trading period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the skewness of asset prices during the last hour of trading, indicating the asymmetry of the price distribution in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the skewness of asset prices during the first hour of trading, indicating the asymmetry of the price distribution in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the skewness of returns during the last hour of trading, indicating the asymmetry of the return distribution in that period. Skewness measures the degree to which the distribution of returns deviates from a normal distribution, providing insights into potential risks and performance characteristics during that trading hour.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the skewness of returns during the first hour of trading, indicating the asymmetry of the return distribution in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the skewness of trading volume during the last hour of the trading session, indicating the asymmetry of volume distribution in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the skewness of trading volume during the first hour of trading, indicating the asymmetry of volume distribution in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the standard deviation of closing prices during the last hour of trading, indicating the volatility of asset prices in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the standard deviation of closing prices during the first hour of trading, indicating the variability of asset prices in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the standard deviation of returns during the last hour of trading, indicating the volatility of asset price movements in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the standard deviation of returns during the first hour of trading, providing insight into the volatility of asset price movements in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the standard deviation of trading volume during the last hour of the trading session, indicating the variability in the number of shares traded in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This metric represents the standard deviation of trading volume during the first hour of trading, providing insights into the variability and liquidity of the asset in that period.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: Total trading volume during the last hour of the trading session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: Total trading volume during the first hour of the trading session.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: The Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) calculated during the last hour of the trading session, providing an average price at which a security has traded throughout that period, weighted by volume.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: The Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) calculated during the first trading hour, providing an average price that reflects the volume of trades executed in that period.

items.author: zliu|zliu|xdu|xdu|xbwang|xbwang|jianggeliu
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the next earnings announcement date for a company.
items.keywords: trading days until next earnings announcement

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable provides a numeric representation of the days of the week, where 1 corresponds to Monday, 2 to Tuesday, and so on through 7 for Sunday.
items.keywords: Numeric representation of days of the week

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the first trading day of the current calendar month, with '0' representing the first trading day itself.
items.keywords: Trading days since the start of the month

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the first trading day of the current calendar quarter. A value of '0' signifies that it is the first trading day of the quarter.
items.keywords: Trading days since the start of the quarter

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the first trading day of the calendar year, with '0' representing that initial trading day.
items.keywords: Trading days since the start of the year

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the last trading holiday.

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the last monthly options expiration date.
items.keywords: Trading days since last options expiration

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days that have elapsed since the last quarterly options expiration date.
items.keywords: Trading days since last quarterly options expiration

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the last trading day of the current calendar month. A value of '0' signifies that today is the last trading day of the month.
items.keywords: Days until last trading day of the month

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the last trading day of the current calendar quarter. A value of '0' signifies that today is the last trading day of the quarter.
items.keywords: Days until last trading day of the quarter

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the last trading day of the calendar year. A value of '0' signifies that it is the last trading day of the year.

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the next scheduled trading holiday in the financial markets.

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the next monthly options expiration date.
items.keywords: Trading days until next options expiration

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable indicates the number of trading days remaining until the next quarterly options expiration date.
items.keywords: Trading days until next quarterly options expiration

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable provides a numeric representation of the months of the year, where each month is assigned a number from 1 to 12 (e.g., 1 for January, 2 for February, etc.).

items.author: jzhou
items.description: This variable provides a numeric representation of the quarter of the year, where 1 represents the first quarter, 2 represents the second quarter, 3 represents the third quarter, and 4 represents the fourth quarter.

items.author: ycai
items.description: This variable represents the daily returns of the GLD ETF, which tracks the price of gold bullion. The return is calculated as the percentage change in the ETF's price from one day to the next.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the 1-day return of the S&P 500 Index (SPX), calculated as the percentage change in the index value from the previous day's close to the current day's close.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the 1-day return of the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), which measures market expectations of near-term volatility based on S&P 500 index options. The return is calculated as the percentage change in the VIX value from one day to the next.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the closing price of the S&P 500 Index (SPX), which is an American stock market index based on the market capitalizations of 500 large companies listed on the NYSE or NASDAQ.

items.author: tpark|aarnold
items.description: This variable represents the closing price of the VIX, which is the ticker symbol for the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) Volatility Index. The VIX reflects the market's expectation of 30-day volatility and is constructed using the implied volatilities of a broad range of S&P 500 index options.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for all items in the United States, not seasonally adjusted, indicating the growth rate compared to the previous period. It reflects changes in the price level of a basket of consumer goods and services, providing insight into inflation trends.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers, covering all items and seasonally adjusted. The index is set to a base value of 100 for the period 1982-1984, providing a measure of inflation and changes in the cost of living over time.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers, excluding food and energy prices. It is seasonally adjusted and indexed to the base period of 1982-1984, where the index value is set to 100. This measure provides insight into inflation trends by focusing on core consumer prices.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers, indicating the purchasing power of the consumer dollar. The index is not seasonally adjusted and is based on the reference period of 1982-1984, where the index value is set to 100.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of the United States, expressed in billions of dollars and seasonally adjusted to reflect annual rates. It provides a comprehensive measure of the economic performance of the country.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of the United States, adjusted for seasonal variations and expressed at an annual rate in billions of chained 2009 dollars. It reflects the total economic output, adjusted for inflation, providing a measure of the economy's performance over time.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) implicit price deflator, which measures the level of prices of all new, domestically produced, final goods and services in an economy. The data is seasonally adjusted and indexed to 2009, where the value for that year is set to 100.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the GDPNow estimate, which indicates the seasonally adjusted annual rate of change in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) expressed as a percentage. It provides a real-time estimate of economic growth based on the latest available data.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for individuals aged 20 years and over, expressed as a percentage. It provides insights into the labor market conditions for this demographic group.
items.keywords: Unemployment Rate for ages 20 and over

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the seasonally adjusted unemployment level in the United States, measured in thousands of persons. It indicates the total number of individuals who are unemployed and actively seeking work, adjusted to account for seasonal fluctuations in employment patterns.

items.author: szhou|tchan
items.description: This variable represents the spot price of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil, measured in dollars per barrel and not seasonally adjusted.
